subject: english
title: Present Simple
description: Habits, facts and schedules — plus the third-person -s that everyone forgets.

content.title: When to use it
content.body: Present Simple describes habits, general truths and timetabled events: I work in Wrocław. Water boils at 100 degrees. The train leaves at seven.

content.title: Form
content.body: Base verb, except in the third person singular, which takes -s: I work / she works. Questions and negatives use do or does, and the main verb goes back to its base form: Does she work? She does not work.

content.title: Watch out
content.body: Never double the marker. "Does she works?" is wrong — does already carries the tense, so the verb stays as work.

exercises.question: Complete the sentence.
exercises.explanation: Third person singular takes -s in Present Simple. A permanent job is a habit, not something happening right now.

exercises.question: Which question is correct?
exercises.explanation: Does carries the third-person marker, so the main verb returns to its base form: work.

exercises.question: Present Simple can describe a future event that runs to a timetable, as in "The train leaves at six".
exercises.explanation: Scheduled events take Present Simple even when they are in the future — timetables, programmes, itineraries.

exercises.question: Translate the sentence.

answers.text: I go to work by tram every day.
I went to work by tram every day.
I have gone to work by tram every day.
I am going to work by tram every day.

exercises.explanation: Codziennie marks a habit, so English uses Present Simple rather than the continuous form.

exercises.question: Complete the negative sentence.
exercises.sentence: He ___ drink coffee in the evening.
exercises.explanation: Third person singular negatives use doesn't plus the base verb.

exercises.question: Where does an adverb of frequency such as "usually" normally go?

answers.text: Before the main verb, but after the verb to be
Always at the end of the sentence

exercises.explanation: I usually start at nine. She is usually late. The rule flips around to be, which is the part most learners miss.

exercises.question: What is the third person singular of "study"?
exercises.explanation: A consonant + y becomes -ies. A vowel + y just takes -s: plays, buys.

exercises.question: Vocabulary
exercises.front: State verbs: know, believe, own, need
exercises.back: Normally used in Present Simple, not in the continuous form
exercises.explanation: "I am knowing the answer" is wrong. State verbs describe a condition rather than an activity in progress.

exercises.question: Complete the sentence.
exercises.explanation: General truths take Present Simple, whatever is happening at the moment of speaking.

exercises.question: Which question is correct?
exercises.explanation: A singular third-person subject takes does, and the main verb stays in its base form.

exercises.question: Translate the sentence.
exercises.sentence: Ona zwykle zaczyna pracę o dziewiątej.

answers.text: She is usually starting work at nine.
She usually starts work at nine.
She usually start work at nine.
She has usually started work at nine.

exercises.explanation: A routine takes Present Simple, the third person takes -s, and usually sits before the main verb.

exercises.question: Complete the sentence.
exercises.sentence: My team ___ a stand-up every morning.
exercises.explanation: Team is treated as singular in American English and commonly in British business writing too, so has is the safe choice.

exercises.question: Both halves of "If you push this button, the test runs" are in Present Simple.
exercises.explanation: The zero conditional describes something always true, and uses Present Simple in both clauses — the standard shape for documentation.

exercises.question: Why is "I am thinking it is a good idea" wrong?

answers.text: Think meaning "have an opinion" is stative, so it takes the simple form
Think can never be used in the continuous

exercises.explanation: "I'm thinking about it" is fine — that is the activity sense. The opinion sense is a state: I think it's a good idea.

exercises.question: Vocabulary
exercises.back: goes · does · watches · fixes — -es after o, ch, sh, s, x, z
exercises.explanation: The rest just take -s. This is the single most common written slip at B2 level.
